extracted.intended_audience: public education personnel (teachers, administrators, community college and university staff) preparing proposals for federal vocational education funds in Florida
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing preliminary and final proposals to the Florida Division of Vocational Education, covering methodology, budget, timelines, evaluation, dissemination, and submission procedures. Focuses on what reviewers expect and how to document planning and management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology section: overall purpose and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Objectives are implemented through methodology. The methodology section should include the plan of the project (procedures) and the organizational and administrative arrangement for conducting the project (project management).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit details to convince the funding agency that the objectives can be accomplished. Describe procedures and project management so reviewers can judge feasibility and organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning technique: problem/objectives/methods/evaluation matrix
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a four-column planning sheet with columns 'problem', 'objectives', 'methods', and 'evaluation' so each objective is tied to the problem, methods, success criteria, and evaluation method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List objectives separately to check (1) contribution to solving the problem, (2) methods to accomplish each objective, (3) criteria of success, and (4) most appropriate evaluation method. This demonstrates effective linkage among problem, objectives, methods, and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology contents: participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the participants (those measured or affected), including number to be selected and eligibility criteria. Consider age, education level, ethnic origin, rurality, socioeconomic level, program participation, and/or sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate what generalizations of findings will apply and guard against bias. Reviewers want to know who will be selected, how they will be selected, and why these persons are important to include.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant selection and sampling rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the pool from which participants will be drawn and the sampling method (e.g., stratified, clustered, random) or rationale for selecting whole units (e.g., a class or program).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a sampling method is used, provide rationale. If entire units are selected, explain reasons. This helps reviewers evaluate representativeness and validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology contents: setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the setting where the project will be conducted (districts, communities, schools, or classes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide demographic characteristics useful for assessing appropriateness of the setting to the project's aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology contents: facilities and equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any special facilities or equipment required to accomplish objectives and the rationale for purchase or rental if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate whether facilities/equipment could be made available by cooperative arrangement. Note that approval for equipment purchases and facility rental is the exception. Ready availability of needed facilities/equipment should be noted if project is to begin shortly after approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities description requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe library, office, or other special facilities which will aid conducting the project, including method and criteria for selecting facilities and how their use will be acquired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment description requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe equipment required for successful completion, including method and criteria for selecting equipment and how its use is to be acquired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects with little or no money budgeted for equipment or facility rental have a better chance of being funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology contents: supplies and materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine consumable supplies and non-consumable materials necessary (e.g., paper, pens, filmstrips, tapes, textbooks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplies/materials info need not appear in narrative but is needed for the budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology contents: staffing
rubrics_metrics.description: List all part- and full-time personnel positions required for administering the project, ensuring the number of staff is realistic and qualifications compatible with scope of work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List assignments by job title and percentage of time each individual will be committed. Name a project director responsible for total administration; include brief statement of director's qualifications in the appendix if identified. Specific names (other than director where appropriate) should be in appendix only because many staff are selected after funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time schedule/timeline: purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: A timeline illustrates anticipated duration of activities, shows order of activities, helps reviewers judge whether objectives can be met in time, and aids external evaluators/monitors in tracking progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include activities in chronological order, person responsible, approximate length of time, beginning and target end dates. Ensure sequence and realistic lapsed times. Timelines may be Gantt charts, PERT charts, flowcharts, or activity-objective listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time schedule/timeline: recommended contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Most time schedules include (1) the activity/function to be performed and (2) the lapsed time from beginning to ending; person/position responsible may be identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be thorough to indicate adequate planning; list activities that lead to objectives and identify responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection and analysis: planning and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan for data collection and analysis early; collected information must be relevant to objectives and a systematic plan for obtaining and interpreting it should be developed to prevent inappropriate data collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection of instruments should be done early. Describe procedures and conditions for collecting data. Inclusion or description of instruments in proposal aids reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection and analysis: validity and reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis and interpretation of data require determination of validity (right things measured) and reliability (consistent measures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no existing instruments exist, adapt or develop them. Identify institutional evaluation or computing specialists who can assist and include them in planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation: purposes and types
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation serves (1) formative feedback for project improvement, (2) monitoring progress relative to timeline, and (3) determining effectiveness in achieving objectives. Evaluation may be internal or external.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include description of methods to measure attainment of objectives. Use objectives as standards for evaluating results. Describe objective evaluation techniques, frequency of evaluation, and who will evaluate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation: recommended objective techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer objective measures over subjective ones; common strategies include interviews, faculty/staff/student reactions, record-keeping (notes, minutes), testing instruments (pre- and post-tests), rating scales/questionnaires/surveys, and outside evaluators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific about data to be collected, collection methods, and criteria for achievement. If evaluation criteria are difficult to determine, reexamine objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe anticipated products/findings, intended audiences, and likely methods to make target groups aware of project results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider dissemination early in project development. The Division may assist in dissemination if awarded, but the proposer should present viable dissemination ideas (e.g., articles to vocational journals, communications to counselors/teachers/administrators).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget: relation to proposal and planning quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The budget contains the best estimate of total cost and breakdown of expenses; it interprets objectives and methodology in monetary terms and reveals the quality of planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure budget categories/expenses relate to project tasks; amounts should be reasonable and adequate for the work. State the time period the budget covers (usually one year); if project spans multiple years, itemize first year and estimate subsequent years. Budgets may be adjusted later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget: fiscal responsibility and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiscal responsibility rests with the contracting institution; projects are subject to institutional, state, and federal audits. Some expenditures are not allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of non-allowable items include alterations of buildings; dues; purchase of equipment not specified in contract/proposal; out-of-state travel without designation; entertainment; contingency/petty cash funds; and dual compensation without prior approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project management: copyright clearance
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain copyright clearance when using or adapting previously developed materials; quoting requires clearance, while developing ideas from literature may not. All materials must be cleared to avoid plagiarism and allow printing/dissemination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copyright clearance steps: (1) receive permission from copyright holders to use/adapt materials; (2) use correct copyright statement to protect State product; (3) determine proper placement of copyright credit lines; (4) document all copyright activities. Project director is responsible for obtaining clearances and documenting them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project monitoring and evaluation by Division
rubrics_metrics.description: State Division personnel will periodically engage in on-site monitoring and evaluation; projects may also be monitored by interdivisional committee representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared for monitoring and provide access/records as required. Consultation with project monitors is part of amendment/change process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project amendment process
rubrics_metrics.description: Revisions to project (personnel, objectives, timeline, budget) may be necessary; consultation with project monitors is required and most updates need Division approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proposed changes contribute to efficiency and obtain required approvals from the Division of Vocational Education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final report: purpose and quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The final report communicates project completion, significant methods/understandings gained, and information useful for future decisions. It should be clear and logical to aid decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final report may accompany products (process models, curriculum guides, evaluation formats). Provide evidence of satisfactory completion and communicate results to interested parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product development and production assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Many projects will produce a tangible product (e.g., curriculum guide, model, catalog). Development of product is the project director's responsibility; production assistance is available from Division bureaus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once product is defined and drafted, assistance may be given in graphics, editing, design, and illustration. Project monitors can advise on production services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary proposal: use of Application for Federal Vocational Funds form
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary proposals must be submitted on the prescribed proposal form in the Application for Federal Vocational Funds; the form standardizes initial submission and screening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary proposals serve as a prospectus-like screening device to save effort before full proposals are prepared. Use the form's instructions and mark NA where items do not apply. Submission must follow institutional channels and include required signatures (e.g., superintendent or president).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission routing and signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are to be routed through the applicant institution (annual plan or amendment) and not submitted directly to the Division. Applications must contain signatures of appropriate chief officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow institutional procedures for clearance and signature before sending. Proposals submitted as amendments should be marked as such and have proper signatures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mini-contract funding specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Mini-contracts provide up to $5,000 per project and cannot be used for regular salaries or equipment. They support innovative classroom/lab/shop ideas applicable statewide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use preliminary proposal form for mini-contracts; funds are from exemplary and innovative categories. Innovative = perceived new idea/concept; exemplary = creative, imaginative, and unique combination of elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to Requests for Proposals (RFPs)
rubrics_metrics.description: An RFP outlines a specific need and the criteria for response; responses should be submitted on the preliminary proposal form with the RFP identification number noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RFP responses follow the same routing and signature requirements and may lead to invitation for a final proposal. Approval of amendments/responses depends on available funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application form completion and category mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: Not all items on the proposal form apply to every funding category; consult Table I (items-to-categories matrix) and preceding instructions to determine what to complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to fill out the form without referring to the instruction manual. Enter NA where items are not applicable.
